skin_texture.roughness_basis: Reconstructed engineering value, not measured from a period person or calibrated capture.
skin_texture.identity_basis: Cleared reusable generic young light-skinned skin atlas (the 1835 studies'); not a likeness, attested complexion, or source identifying any resident.
skin_texture.uv_status: Source atlas and UV registration viewed in source diagnostics; final Blender export/LOD render validation remains outstanding.

hair_component.appearance_basis: Shared cleared CC0 short04 cap, kept as the skull surface the strand hair grows from; no hairstyle or likeness is asserted by the cap.

eye_components.source_basis: Actual helper centers/axes; original opaque sclera/iris/pupil, reconstructed dimensions and brown color, not resident facts

label: Reconstructed 1904 stable helper's working dress (striped shirt in shirt sleeves, black braces, leather belt, dark trousers, brown work boots, light felt hat) on the shared portable male rig
basis: Original shirt and braces shells offset from the cleared adult body's own surface, trousers on the shared workwear shell, a belt lofted round the trousers, a felt hat seated round the skull and closed boots round the feet, cut after the groom's working dress the reference photograph shows (T-3484). Seams, ease, lengths and colours are reconstructed. Complete source anatomy remains unchanged beneath clothing.
source_scope: Frances Benjamin Johnston's photograph of a groom at a horse's head at Tuskegee (ca. 1902, LOC) shows a stable hand at work in his shirt sleeves: a striped shirt with the collar closed, braces, a belt, dark trousers long over his shoes and a light felt hat with a creased crown. The chapter on coachmen and stablemen in Mrs. Seely's Cook Book (1902) says what such a helper's work was: cleaning and harnessing the horses, cleaning the stable and the carriages. Neither is of Chicago or of Billings; the photograph is monochrome; no pixels or traced shapes enter the asset.

body_parameters.height_basis: The shared engineering body; the variation kit draws height and build at runtime. Not a recorded height.
body_parameters.age_basis: Engineering body at the kit base age 35; human-variation.js ages him from his record (born January 1875, 29 in July 1904).
body_parameters.shape_basis: CC0 male macro targets; equal software-category blend is engineering only, not inferred ancestry or a portrait.

proof_variants.body_basis: CC0 adult-male graphical body and the shared young light-skinned generic skin of the 1835 studies are reconstructed authoring choices. August Billings is an inferred person (the 1900 census enumerates him as a helper in the rear building behind the Glessner house); no picture of him is known, and no complexion, height, face or outfit of his is asserted.

stable_helper_components.evidence_choice: The brief allowed shirt sleeves, a waistcoat, work trousers and a cap, whatever the references support. The one photograph read of a groom at work in these years shows him without coat or waistcoat, in a striped shirt with braces and a belt and a light felt hat, not a cap; every piece follows it. It differs from the 1835 labourer's shirt, open waistcoat, neckerchief and slouch hat.

provenance.source_scope: The groom works in his shirt sleeves, without coat or waistcoat, in a pale shirt with a fine stripe, long sleeves buttoned at the wrist and a tall white standing collar closed at the throat. The stripe is not modelled and the collar is drawn in the shirt's colour: the shirt is drawn in a pale blue-grey (reconstructed).
Dark braces over the shoulders, as the groom wears them; their width and the H at the back are reconstructed.
A belt at the trousers' waist worn with the braces, as the groom's; brown leather is reconstructed.
Dark straight trousers long over the shoes, as the groom's; the cloth and its near-black are reconstructed.
Only the shoes' toes show under the groom's trousers; brown laced work boots are a reconstructed choice.
A light felt hat with a creased crown and a short brim, as the groom's; its height, crease and light fawn are reconstructed.
